47935-fathers-and-sons.title: Fathers And Sons
47935-fathers-and-sons.creator: Unknown
47935-fathers-and-sons.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. of about two hundred souls (or, as, after that he had apportioned his peasantry allotments, and set up a "farm," he himself expressed it, a property "of two thousand _desiatini_"[2]). His father, one of the generals of 1812, had spent his life exclusively in military service as the commander, first of a brigade, and then of a division; and always he had been quartered in the provinces, where his rank had enabled him to cut a not inconspicuous figure.

arxiv-1910-13405.title: Experimental Comparison of Bohm-like Theories with Different Primary Ontologies
arxiv-1910-13405.creator: Arthur O. T. Pang, Hugo Ferretti, Noah Lupu-Gladstein, Weng-Kian Tham, Aharon Brodutch, Kent Bonsma-Fisher, J. E. Sipe, Aephraim M. Steinberg
arxiv-1910-13405.description: Abstract The de Broglie-Bohm theory is a hidden-variable interpretation of quantum mechanics which involves particles moving through space along deterministic trajectories. This theory singles out position as the primary ontological variable. Mathematically, it is possible to construct a similar theory where particles are moving through momentum-space, and momentum is singled out as the primary ontological variable.

arxiv-2012-08872.title: Robust self-triggered DMPC for linear discrete-time systems with local and global constraints
arxiv-2012-08872.creator: Zhengcai Li a , Changbing Ma a and Huiling Xu a
arxiv-2012-08872.description: Abstract This paper proposes a robust self-triggered distributed model predictive control (DMPC) scheme for a family of Discrete-Time linear systems with local (uncoupled) and global (coupled) constraints. To handle the additive disturbance, tube-based method is proposed for the satisfaction of local state and control constraints. Meanwhile, A special form of constraints tightening is given to guranteen the global coupled constraints.

arxiv-2105-08903.title: Reaction cross section of proton scattering consistent with PREX-II
arxiv-2105-08903.creator: Tomotsugu Wakasa, Shingo Tagami, Jun Matsui, Masanobu Yahiro, Maya Takechi
arxiv-2105-08903.description: Abstract Background The neutron skin thickness R skin PV R_{\rm skin}^{\rm PV} of PREX-II is presented in Phys. Rev. Lett. 126 , 172502 (2021). The reaction cross section σ R \sigma_{R} is useful to determine the matter radius R m R_{m} and R skin R_{\rm skin} .

arxiv-2106-15274.title: Autonomous Driving Implementation in an Experimental Environment namig.aliyev@ogr.sakarya.edu.tr oguzhan.sezer1@ogr.sakarya.edu.tr mehmet.guzel@ogr.sakarya.edu.tr
arxiv-2106-15274.creator: Namig Aliyev ID, Oguzhan Sezer ID, Mehmet Turan Guzel ID
arxiv-2106-15274.description: Abstract Autonomous systems require identifying the environment and it has a long way to go before putting it safely into practice. In autonomous driving systems, the detection of obstacles and traffic lights are of importance as well as lane tracking. In this study, an autonomous driving system is developed and tested in the experimental environment designed for this purpose.

arxiv-2208-04084.title: Semiclassical strong-field theory of phase delays in ω − 2 ​ ω \omega-2\omega above-threshold ionization
arxiv-2208-04084.creator: Diego G. Arbó 1,2 , Sebastián D. López 1 , {}^{1}, and Joachim Burgdörfer 3
arxiv-2208-04084.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Diego G. Arbó 1,2 , Sebastián D. López 1 , {}^{1}, and Joachim Burgdörfer 3. Phase and time delays of atomic above-threshold ionization were recently experimentally explored in an ω − 2 ​ ω \omega-2\omega setting [Zipp et al , Optica 1 , 361 (2014)]. The phases of wavepackets ejected from argon by a strong 2 ​ ω 2\omega pulse were probed as a function of the relative phase of a weaker ω \omega probe pulse.

arxiv-2208-05212.title: Centrality and Transverse Spherocity dependent study of charged-particle production in Xe-Xe collisions at s N ​ N \sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.44 TeV using PYTHIA8 Angantyr and AMPT models
arxiv-2208-05212.creator: Randhir Singh 1 , Renu Bala 1 , Sanjeev Singh Sambyal 1
arxiv-2208-05212.description: Abstract Transverse Spherocity is an event structure variable which provide an effective way to disentangle the data into hard and soft components of the processes corresponding to events with small and large numbers of multi-parton interactions (MPI), respectively. Recent experimental results in small systems from the LHC suggest the importacnce of transverse spherocity variable in the classification of the events.

arxiv-2211-05049.title: Precision Measurements of Atom-Dimer Interactions in a Uniform Planar Bose Gas
arxiv-2211-05049.creator: C. Maury, B. Bakkali-Hassani, G. Chauveau, F. Rabec, S. Nascimbene, J. Dalibard, J. Beugnon
arxiv-2211-05049.description: Abstract Cold quantum gases, when acted upon by electromagnetic fields, can give rise to samples where isolated atoms coexist with dimers or trimers, which raises the question of the interactions between these various constituents. Here we perform microwave photoassociation in a degenerate gas of 87 Rb atoms to create weakly-bound dimers in their electronic ground state.

arxiv-2305-13945.title: Open Access Improves the Dissemination of Science: Insights from Wikipedia
arxiv-2305-13945.creator: Puyu Yang, Ahad Shoaib, Robert West, Giovanni Colavizza
arxiv-2305-13945.description: Abstract Wikipedia is a well-known platform for disseminating knowledge, and scientific sources, such as journal articles, play a critical role in supporting its mission. The open access movement aims to make scientific knowledge openly available, and we might intuitively expect open access to help further Wikipedia’s mission. However, the extent of this relationship remains largely unknown.

arxiv-2306-10433.title: Star-formation driven outflows in local dwarf galaxies as revealed from [CII] observations by Herschel Thanks: Herschel is an ESA space observatory with science instruments provided by European-led Principal Investigator consortia and with important participation from NASA.
arxiv-2306-10433.creator: M. Romano, A. Nanni, D. Donevski, M. Ginolfi, G. C. Jones, I. Shivaei, Junais, D. Salak, P. Sawant
arxiv-2306-10433.description: Abstract We characterize the physical properties of star-formation driven outflows in a sample of 29 local dwarf galaxies drawn from the Dwarf Galaxy Survey. We make use of Herschel /PACS archival data to search for atomic outflow signatures in the wings of individual [CII] 158 μ \mu m spectra and in their stacked line profile.

arxiv-2402-08260.title: The perturbation method applied to a robust optimization problem with constraint
arxiv-2402-08260.creator: Peng Luo, Alexander Schied, Xiaole Xue
arxiv-2402-08260.description: Abstract Abstract . The present paper studies a kind of robust optimization problems with constraint. The problem is formulated through Backward Stochastic Differential Equations (BSDEs) with quadratic generators. A necessary condition is established for the optimal solution using a terminal perturbation method and properties of Bounded Mean Oscillation (BMO) martingales.

arxiv-2404-14245.title: Functional Closure Properties of Finite ℕ \mathbb{N} -weighted Automata
arxiv-2404-14245.creator: Julian Dörfler, Christian Ikenmeyer
arxiv-2404-14245.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julian Dörfler, Christian Ikenmeyer. We determine all functional closure properties of finite ℕ \mathbb{N} -weighted automata, even all multivariate ones, and in particular all multivariate polynomials. We also determine all univariate closure properties in the promise setting, and all multivariate closure properties under certain assumptions on the promise, in particular we determine all multivariate closure properties where the output vector lies on a monotone algebraic graph variety.

arxiv-2501-17477.title: Bacterial dimensions sensitively regulate surface diffusivity and residence time
arxiv-2501-17477.creator: Premkumar Leishangthem, Xuan Wang, Junan Chen, Shengqi Yang, Xinliang Xu
arxiv-2501-17477.description: Abstract Run-and-tumble is a common but vital strategy that bacteria employ to explore environment suffused with boundaries, as well as to escape from entrapment. In this study we reveal how this strategy and the resulting dynamical behavior can be sensitively regulated by bacterial dimensions.

arxiv-2503-14298.title: Recursive Self-Similarity in Deep Weight Spaces of Neural Architectures: A Fractal and Coarse Geometry Perspective
arxiv-2503-14298.creator: Ambarish Moharil, Indika Kumara, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Majid Mohammadi, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel
arxiv-2503-14298.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ambarish Moharil, Indika Kumara, Damian Andrew Tamburri, Majid Mohammadi, Willem-Jan van den Heuvel. This paper conceptualizes the Deep Weight Spaces (DWS) of neural architectures as hierarchical, fractal -like, coarse geometric structures observable at discrete integer scales through recursive dilation.

arxiv-2506-22328.title: A free boundary approach to non-scattering obstacles with vanishing contrast
arxiv-2506-22328.creator: Mikko Salo, Henrik Shahgholian
arxiv-2506-22328.description: Abstract . Motivated by questions in inverse scattering theory, we develop free boundary methods in obstacle problems where both the solution and the right hand side of the equation may have varying sign. The key condition that prevents the appearance of corners is that the right hand side should be related to a harmonic polynomial.

arxiv-2508-17281.title: From Language to Action: A Review of Large Language Models as Autonomous Agents and Tool Users
arxiv-2508-17281.creator: Sadia Sultana Chowa 1 , Riasad Alvi 2 , Subhey Sadi Rahman 2 , Md Abdur Rahman 2 , Mohaimenul Azam Khan Raiaan 2 , Md Rafiqul Islam 3 , Mukhtar Hussain 3 , Sami Azam 3,* 1 Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Daffodil International University, Dhaka-1341, Bangladesh 2 Department of Comput
arxiv-2508-17281.description: Abstract The pursuit of human-level artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly advanced the development of autonomous agents and Large Language Models (LLMs). LLMs are now widely utilized as decision-making agents for their ability to interpret instructions, manage sequential tasks, and adapt through feedback.

arxiv-2509-04495.title: I. Linear Interacting Dark Energy: Analytical Solutions and Theoretical Pathologies
arxiv-2509-04495.creator: Marcel van der Westhuizen, Amare Abebe, Eleonora Di Valentino
arxiv-2509-04495.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marcel van der Westhuizen, Amare Abebe, Eleonora Di Valentino. Interacting dark energy (IDE) models, in which dark matter (DM) and dark energy (DE) exchange energy through a non-gravitational interaction, have long been proposed as candidates to address key challenges in modern cosmology. These include the coincidence problem, the H 0 H_{0} and S 8 S_{8} tensions, and, more recently, the hints of dynamical dark energy reported by the DESI collaboration.

arxiv-2509-07160.title: Safe cross-entropy-based importance sampling for rare event simulations
arxiv-2509-07160.creator: Zhiwei Gao, George Karniadakis
arxiv-2509-07160.description: Abstract The Improved Cross-Entropy (ICE) method is a powerful tool for estimating failure probabilities in reliability analysis. Its core idea is to approximate the optimal importance-sampling density by minimizing the forward Kullback–Leibler divergence within a chosen parametric family—typically a mixture model. However, conventional mixtures are often light-tailed, which leads to slow convergence and instability when targeting very small failure probabilities.

arxiv-2511-01532.title: On acyclic b-chromatic number of cubic graphs
arxiv-2511-01532.creator: Marcin Anholcer, Sylwia Cichacz, Iztok Peterin
arxiv-2511-01532.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Marcin Anholcer, Sylwia Cichacz, Iztok Peterin. An acyclic k k -coloring of G G is a map c : V ⁡ ( G ) → { 1 , … , k } c:V(G)\rightarrow\{1,\dots,k\} such that c ⁡ ( u ) ≠ c ⁡ ( v ) c(u)\neq c(v) for any u ​ v ∈ E ⁡ ( G ) uv\in E(G) and the subgraph induced by the vertices of any two colors i , j ∈ { 1 , … , k } i,j\in\{1,\dots,k\}

arxiv-2511-20120.title: AiMNLP at BHASHA Task 1 IndicGEC: “When Data is Scarce, Prompt Smarter”… Approaches to Grammatical Error Correction in Low-Resource Settings
arxiv-2511-20120.creator: Somsubhra De, Harsh Kumar, Arun Prakash A
arxiv-2511-20120.description: Abstract Grammatical error correction (GEC) is an important task in Natural Language Processing that aims to automatically detect and correct grammatical mistakes in text. While recent advances in transformer-based models and large annotated datasets have greatly improved GEC performance for high-resource languages such as English, the progress has not extended equally.

arxiv-2512-19376.title: A Critical Assessment of Pattern Comparisons Between POD and Autoencoders in Intraventricular Flows Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2512-19376.creator: E. Lazpita, A. Bell-Navas, J. Garicano-Mena, P. Koumoutsakos, S. Le Clainche
arxiv-2512-19376.description: Abstract Understanding intraventricular hemodynamics requires compact and physically interpretable representations of the underlying flow structures, as characteristic flow patterns are closely associated with cardiovascular conditions and can support the early detection of cardiac deterioration. Conventional visualization of velocity or pressure fields, however, provides limited insight into the coherent mechanisms driving these dynamics.

arxiv-2601-06825.title: Quarkonium light-cone distribution amplitudes: twist structure and mass dependence
arxiv-2601-06825.creator: Shuai Xu, Xiao-Nan Li, Jin-Zhong Han, Bai-hui Cheng, Li-li Chen, Qin Chang
arxiv-2601-06825.description: Abstract We present a systematic study of the leading- and next-to-leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) of ground-state pseudoscalar and vector quarkonium within the light-front quark model (LFQM). By implementing the replacement M → M 0 M\to M_{0} , we analyze the longitudinal and transverse structures of the LCDAs, together with their Gegenbauer moments, ξ \xi -moments, and transverse momentum moments.

arxiv-2601-11195.title: Beyond Validity: SVAR Identification Through the Proxy Zoo Thanks: Contacts: Jiaming Huang ( jiaminghuang@ust.hk ) and Luca Neri ( luca.neri@uclouvain.be ). We would like to thank Luca Fanelli, Byoungchan Lee, and seminar participants at CUHK Shenzhen, 2025 Annual Meeting of the Greater Bay Economet
arxiv-2601-11195.creator: Jiaming Huang, Luca Neri
arxiv-2601-11195.description: Abstract This paper develops a framework for robust identification in SVARs when researchers face a zoo of proxy variables. Instead of imposing exact exogeneity, we introduce generalized ranking restrictions (GRR) that bound the relative correlation of each proxy with the target and non-target shocks through a continuous proxy-quality parameter.

arxiv-2601-14260.title: End-to-End Transformer Acceleration Through Processing-in-Memory Architectures
arxiv-2601-14260.creator: Xiaoxuan Yang, Peilin Chen, Tergel Molom-Ochir, Yiran ChenEmail: {xiaoxuan, peilin}@virginia.edu, {tm431, yiran.chen}@duke.edu
arxiv-2601-14260.description: Abstract Transformers have become central to natural language processing and large language models, but their deployment at scale faces three major challenges. First, the attention mechanism requires massive matrix multiplications and frequent movement of intermediate results between memory and compute units, leading to high latency and energy costs.

arxiv-2603-09004.title: Can AI Agents Generate Microservices? How Far are We?
arxiv-2603-09004.creator: Bassam Adnan, Matteo Esposito, Davide Taibi, Karthik Vaidhyanathan

arxiv-2604-00721.title: A column generation algorithm for finding co-3-plexes in chordal graphs Journal: Discrete optimization
arxiv-2604-00721.creator: Alexandre Dupont-Bouillard

plaw-107-146-2002.title: An act to designate the United States Post Office located at 60 Third Avenue in Long Branch, New Jersey, as the "Pat King Post Office Building".
plaw-107-146-2002.creator: United States Congress
plaw-107-146-2002.description: Public Law 107-146 (2002): An act to designate the United States Post Office located at 60 Third Avenue in Long Branch, New Jersey, as the "Pat King Post Office Building".

pmc-10547552.title: Dominance of photo over chromatic acclimation strategies by habitat-forming mesophotic red algae
pmc-10547552.creator: Sofie E. Voerman, Beauregard C. Marsh, Ricardo G. Bahia, Guilherme H. Pereira-Filho, Ana Clara F. Becker, Gilberto M. Amado-Filho, Arvydas Ruseckas, Graham A. Turnbull, Ifor D. W. Samuel, Heidi L. Burdett
pmc-10547552.description: Red coralline algae are the deepest living macroalgae, capable of creating spatially complex reefs from the intertidal to 100+ m depth with global ecological and biogeochemical significance. How these algae maintain photosynthetic function under increasingly limiting light intensity and spectral availability is key to explaining their large depth distribution.

pmc-11360563.title: Exploring Virus Diversity in the Potato leafhopper (Empoasca fabae), an Economically Important Agricultural Pest
pmc-11360563.creator: Thanuja Thekke-Veetil, Doris Lagos-Kutz, Leslie L. Domier, Nancy K. McCoppin, Glen L. Hartman, Steven J. Clough
pmc-11360563.description: The potato leafhopper (Empoasca fabae, PLH) is a serious pest that feeds on a wide range of agricultural crops and is found throughout the United States but is not known to be a vector for plant-infecting viruses. We probed the diversity of virus sequences in field populations of PLH collected from four Midwestern states: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, and Minnesota.

pmc-12469874.title: Sex and Gender Influences on the Impacts of Disasters: A Rapid Review of Evidence
pmc-12469874.creator: Carol Muñoz-Nieves, Lorraine Greaves, Ella Huber, Andreea C Brabete, Lindsay Wolfson, Nancy Poole, Eleanor Holroyd, Alessandro Miani, William A Toscano
pmc-12469874.description: Both sex-related factors and gender-related factors affect the immediate and long term mental and physical health impacts of disasters, including those resulting from public health emergencies, climate-related events, and naturally occurring phenomena. These include sex-specific biological, physiological and genetic processes, mechanisms underlying reproduction, disease outcomes, and stress, immune, and trauma responses.

pmc-12528399.title: DynaRNA: accurate dynamic RNA conformation ensemble generation with diffusion model
pmc-12528399.creator: Zhengxin Li, Junjie Zhu, Xiaokun Hong, Junxi Mu, Zhuoqi Zheng, Taeyoung Cui, Yutong Sun, Ting Wei, Hai-Feng Chen
pmc-12528399.description: RNA plays a wide variety of roles in biological processes. In addition to serving as the coding messenger RNA (mRNA), the vast majority of RNAs function as non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs), where their dynamic structural ensemble is critical for mediating diverse biological functions.

pmc-12530365.title: Comparative effectiveness of take-home dosing schedules for opioid agonist treatment in British Columbia, Canada: a target trial emulation protocol using a population-based observational study
pmc-12530365.creator: Megan Kurz, B Carolina Guerra-Alejos, Md Belal Hossain, Jeong Eun Min, Ruyu Yan, Julie Bruneau, Nicole L A Catherine, Sander Greenland, Paul Gustafson, Lindsay Hedden, Ehsan Karim, Lawrence McCandless, Seonaid Nolan, Robert W Platt, Paxton Bach, Shaun Seaman, U Siebert, M Eugenia Socías, Bohdan Nosy
pmc-12530365.description: AbstractIntroductionThe introduction of fentanyl and its analogues in the illicit drug supply has prompted greater emphasis on refining clinical treatment protocols to ensure sustained retention in opioid agonist treatment (OAT). Take-home dosing may lessen the treatment burden on clients and thus reduce the risk of treatment discontinuation.

pmc-12732691.title: Bacterial Profile, Molecular Serotyping, and Key Genetic Determinants for Adhesion, Immune Evasion, and Tissue Spread Among Bulgarian Children with Acute Otitis Media
pmc-12732691.creator: Alexandra S. Alexandrova, Vasil S. Boyanov, Raina T. Gergova
pmc-12732691.description: Background: Acute otitis media (AOM) is one of the most common pediatric infections. We aimed to investigate the bacterial profile of AOM in children, the serotype distribution, and the main genetic virulence factors involved in adhesion, immune evasion, and tissue spread. Methods: In total, 121 AOM cases involving children aged 0 to 14 years were studied.

pmc-12770569.title: Repurposing antibacterial drugs identifies ridinilazole and CRS3123 as promising candidates against vancomycin-resistant enterococci
pmc-12770569.creator: Somaia M Abdelmegeed, Mohamed F Mohamed, Mohamed N Seleem
pmc-12770569.description: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) represent a growing threat to public health due to their increasing prevalence and limited treatment options. The urgent need for alternative therapeutics highlights the value of novel approaches such as drug repurposing to identify effective antimicrobial agents. In this study, we screened a library of 1,135 antibacterial compounds to identify candidates active against VRE.

pmc-12966223.title: A comparison of single-domain and multidomain executive functions cognitive training for enhancing cognition and well-being in older adults
pmc-12966223.creator: Lan Nguyen, Karen Murphy, Glenda Andrews, Amanda Duffy
pmc-12966223.description: This study investigated the efficacy of single-domain (working memory; WM) and multidomain core executive functions (EFs; cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, WM) cognitive training programs in enhancing cognitive performance (measured objectively and subjectively) and well-being. Participants comprised 66 healthy older adults (Mage = 69.58, SD = 7.04) who were assigned to a 4-week single-domain WM, multidomain EF, or active control program.

pmc-13287198.title: Impact of Single-Inhaler Triple Therapy FF/UMEC/VI on Disease Stability in COPD: A Real-World 12-Month Analysis
pmc-13287198.creator: Chiara Lupia, Daniela Pastore, Antonio Giacalone, Federica Marrelli, Lucia Novelli, Debbie Riccelli, Angelantonio Maglio, Giuseppe Armentaro, Angela Sciacqua, Alessandro Vatrella, Girolamo Pelaia, Corrado Pelaia
pmc-13287198.description: IntroductionSingle-inhaler triple therapy with fluticasone furoate/umeclidinium/vilanterol (FF/UMEC/VI) is recommended for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who remain symptomatic or experience exacerbations despite dual bronchodilation. However, real-world evidence on its ability to achieve multidimensional “disease stability”, integrating symptoms, lung function, and exacerbation outcomes, remains limited.

pmc-13385098.title: Ergonomic risk assessment in municipal waste management: integrating standardized methods with real-world context
pmc-13385098.creator: Vincenzo Cianci, Daniela Sapienza, Simone De Sio, Hector Nieto, Gabriella Martino, Concetto Mario Giorgianni
pmc-13385098.description: IntroductionManual handling of loads (MHL) represents a relevant occupational risk in the waste management sector, where lifting, pushing, and pulling are performed daily under variable and often complex operational conditions. This study aimed to assess ergonomic risk in a municipal waste management company through the application of standardized methods and to evaluate their utility for preventive decision-making in real-world contexts.

pmc-13557536.title: Impact of Co-Supplementation of Gallic Acid With Vitamin C on Oxidant Stress, Inflammation, Hepatic and Renal Histology of Type 2 Diabetic Rats Induced With Fructose and Streptozotocin
pmc-13557536.creator: Shufang YAN, Xu XIANG, Wei HUA
pmc-13557536.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryThis study assessed the impact of gallic acid plus vitamin C on systemic oxidant stress, inflammation, hepatic and renal histology of rats with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Twenty five albino male rats were allotted into five categories of five rats each and treated hereafter as: control and diabetic group (fed rat diets and water), vitamin C (diabetic treated rats administered vitamin C, 50 mg/kg), gallic acid (diabetic treated rats administered gallic acid at 20 mg/kg), gallic acid plus vitamin C (diabetic treated

pmc-13610749.title: Comparative evaluation of anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects of prasugrel versus clopidogrel in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: A prospective cohort study
pmc-13610749.creator: Shanmugapriya Vinayagam, Niti Mittal, Ashwani Kumar, Manjulata Kumawat, Aparna Parmar, Vijay Kalra, Joshuah Jebaraj
pmc-13610749.description: BACKGROUND:While both clopidogrel and prasugrel inhibit platelet aggregation, their comparative pleiotropic effects on inflammatory and oxidative stress markers remain unclear.OBJECTIVE:To compare the anti-inflammatory and antioxidant potential of clopidogrel and prasugrel given as dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) along with aspirin in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
